---
title: "simstim setup"
---

<!-- Generated by `just docs` from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

Set up step by step: a host, its agents, and their logins.

```text
simstim setup [flags]
```

A guided setup. It asks where agents will run: a host in your SSH config, a local VM with Lima, a Docker container, an E2B sandbox, or a server you will rent, which it walks you through. It connects or creates the host, installs the agents you tick with their official installers, and offers each agent's own login, each in a session you watch. Ctrl+C stops it at any step, and it says what was done.

Without a terminal, name the host with `--host` or `--create`, and pass `--yes`.

## Examples

```sh
simstim setup
simstim setup --host my-server --agents claude,codex
simstim setup --create lima --agents claude --yes --no-login
```

## Flags

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--agents <string>` | the agents to install, such as claude,codex (none installs nothing) |
| `--create <string>` | make a new host with a provider: lima, docker or e2b |
| `--host <string>` | use this host: a saved host, a Host from your SSH config, or user@host |
| `--name <string>` | the host's name (default: from `--host`, or the provider's name) |
| `--no-login` | do not offer the agents' logins |
| `-y`, `--yes` | do not ask: install the helper, and only the agents in `--agents` |

## Flags from the parent command

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--debug[=<categories>]` | turn on the debug mode, with every category, or with the categories listed: attach, net, memory, launcher, runtime. A list binds only in the = form, such as `--debug=net` |
| `--debug-file <file>` | write the client's debug records to this file. On its own, it turns on every category (SIMSTIM_DEBUG_FILE does the same) |
